body.heading: Where in the world is Iceland?
paragraphs: Iceland is a country in Northern Europe, which is part of Europe. It is an island country, surrounded by sea.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Iceland is Reykjavik.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Iceland is Icelandic.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Iceland is the Icelandic króna.

body.heading: How big is Iceland?
paragraphs: Iceland covers about 103,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Belarus.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where tectonic plates spread apart. That means Iceland is slowly growing wider — the two sides of the island are drifting apart by a few centimetres every year.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Iceland's Golden Circle packs wonders into one loop: a rift valley where continents drift apart, erupting geysers and the mighty Gullfoss waterfall.
At Jökulsárlón, blue icebergs calve from a glacier and float to a black-sand beach, glittering like diamonds — seals swim among them.
